nodes.summary: If `(Q, P)` is incentive compatible on `[a, b]`, then `Q` is monotone on `[a, b]` (Myerson 1981, (4.2); Nisan 2007, Theorem 9.39 (i)).
nodes.title: Monotonicity of incentive-compatible allocations

nodes.summary: If `(Q, P)` is incentive compatible on `[a, b]`, then `U t = U a + ∫_a^t Q` for every `t ∈ [a, b]` (Myerson 1981, (4.3)).
nodes.title: Envelope formula

nodes.summary: If `g` is monotone on `[a, b]` and the increments of `D` satisfy `|D t - D s| ≤ (g t - g s) * (t - s)` for `a ≤ s ≤ t ≤ b`, then `D b = D a`: summing over a partition of `[a, b]` into `n` equal pieces bounds `|D b - D a|` by `(g b - g a) * (b - a) / n`.
nodes.title: Two-sided comparison lemma

nodes.summary: If `0 ≤ Q` on `[a, b]` and `a ≤ b`, the mechanism `(Q, P)` is incentive compatible and individually rational (`U t ≥ 0` for all `t ∈ [a, b]`) on `[a, b]` if and only if `Q` is monotone on `[a, b]`, the envelope formula `U t = U a + ∫_a^t Q` holds on `[a, b]`, and `U a ≥ 0` (Myerson 1981, Lemma 2, (4.2)–(4.4), for a single bidder without revision effects; the probability conditions (3.3) are the separate hypothesis…
nodes.title: Myerson's Lemma 2 for one bidder

nodes.summary: Incentive compatibility is equivalent to `U s + (t - s) * Q s ≤ U t` for all `s, t ∈ [a, b]` (Myerson 1981, (4.6)).
nodes.title: Myerson's inequality (4.6)

nodes.summary: The single-parameter mechanism `(Q, P)` is incentive compatible on `[a, b]` if and only if `Q` is monotone on `[a, b]` and `U t = U a + ∫_a^t Q` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`, where `U t = t * Q t - P t` (Myerson 1981, Lemma 2, conditions (4.2) and (4.3); Nisan 2007, Theorem 9.39; Hartline and Karlin 2007, Theorem 13.6). No regularity of `Q` beyond monotonicity is needed.
nodes.title: Myerson's lemma

nodes.summary: The single-parameter mechanism `(Q, P)` is incentive compatible on `[a, b]`: for all values `s, t ∈ [a, b]`, an agent of value `t` does not gain by reporting `s`, that is `t * Q s - P s ≤ t * Q t - P t` (Myerson 1981, (3.5) without revision effects; Hartline and Karlin 2007, Definition 13.5).
nodes.title: Incentive compatibility on an interval

nodes.summary: Two single-parameter mechanisms with the same allocation rule `Q` that are incentive compatible on `[a, b]` and charge the same payment at the lowest value `a` charge the same payment at every value in `[a, b]` (the one-bidder form of Myerson 1981, Corollary; Nisan 2007, Theorem 9.46).
nodes.title: Revenue equivalence (pointwise)

nodes.summary: In an incentive-compatible single-parameter mechanism on `[a, b]`, the payment is determined by the allocation rule and the utility of the lowest value: `P t = t * Q t - ∫_a^t Q - U a` (Myerson 1981, (4.8) with `U a = 0`; Hartline and Karlin 2007, Theorem 13.6 (ii), where `a = 0` and `P 0 = 0`).
nodes.title: Payment formula

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `payment_eqOn_of_isIncentiveCompatibleOn`, the expected payments agree for every distribution `μ` of values: `∫_{[a,b]} P₁ dμ = ∫_{[a,b]} P₂ dμ` (the one-bidder form of Myerson 1981, Corollary: the seller's expected revenue is determined by the allocation rule and the utilities of the lowest types).
nodes.title: Revenue equivalence (in expectation)

nodes.summary: The utility `t * Q t - P t` of an agent of value `t` reporting truthfully to the single-parameter mechanism with allocation `Q` and payment `P`.
nodes.title: Truthful utility

nodes.summary: Under incentive compatibility on `[a, b]`, `U s + (t - s) * Q s ≤ U t` for `s, t ∈ [a, b]`.
nodes.title: Myerson's inequality, applied

nodes.summary: If `(Q, P)` is incentive compatible on `[a, b]`, `Q ≥ 0` on `[a, b]` and the lowest value gets `U a ≥ 0`, then every value gets a nonnegative utility (Myerson 1981, proof of Lemma 2: (3.4) follows from (4.3) and (4.4)).
nodes.title: Individual rationality from the lowest type

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
